ollama.title: Ollama CORS Setup Required
ollama.content:
Ollama requires CORS permissions to accept requests from browser extensions.

**Windows (PowerShell as Administrator):**
```powershell
# For Chrome extensions
setx OLLAMA_ORIGINS "chrome-extension://*" /M

# For Firefox extensions
setx OLLAMA_ORIGINS "moz-extension://*" /M

# Or allow all origins (development only)
setx OLLAMA_ORIGINS "*" /M
```

**macOS/Linux:**
```bash
# Add to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc
export OLLAMA_ORIGINS="chrome-extension://*"
# Or for all origins (development only)
export OLLAMA_ORIGINS="*"
```

After setting the environment variable:
1. Restart your terminal
2. Start Ollama: `ollama serve`
3. Pull a model: `ollama pull llama3.2`

lmstudio.title: LM Studio Setup
lmstudio.content:
LM Studio provides an OpenAI-compatible local server.

**Setup:**
1. Download and install [LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai)
2. Download a model from the Discover tab
3. Go to Local Server tab
4. Click **Start Server** (default port: 1234)
5. Copy the server URL shown

**Note:** No CORS setup needed — works out of the box with extensions.

jan.title: JAN Setup
jan.content:
JAN (Just Another Network) is an OpenAI-compatible local AI server.

**Setup:**
1. Download [JAN](https://jan.ai)
2. Install and launch the app
3. Go to **Settings** → **Extensions** → **Local API Server**
4. Enable the API server (default port: 1337)
5. Download a model from the Hub

**Default endpoint:** `http://localhost:1337`

unsloth.title: Unsloth Desktop Setup
unsloth.content:
Unsloth Desktop runs OpenAI-compatible API server for local LLMs.

**Setup:**
1. Download [Unsloth Desktop](https://unsloth.ai/download)
2. Launch the app
3. Create a **Access Token** in Settings → API, put your token name and click Generate
4. Start the server (default port: 8888)
5. Use Generated Token for Bearer API Key.

llamacpp.title: llama.cpp Setup
llamacpp.content:
llama.cpp provides OpenAI-compatible API via its server binary.

**Setup:**
1. Clone/download [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp)
2. Build the server: `make` or `cmake`
3. Download a GGUF model
4. Start server:
   ```bash
   ./llama-server -m model.gguf --port 8080
   ```

**Endpoint:** Use `/v1/chat/completions` path.

koboldcpp.title: KoboldCpp Setup
koboldcpp.content:
KoboldCpp offers OpenAI-compatible endpoint at `/v1`.

**Setup:**
1. Download [KoboldCpp](https://github.com/lostruins/koboldcpp)
2. Launch with a GGUF model:
   ```bash
   koboldcpp.exe model.gguf --port 5001
   ```
3. Access web UI at `http://localhost:5001`

**API endpoint:** `http://localhost:5001/v1`

**Note:** Use `/v1` path for OpenAI compatibility.

localai.title: LocalAI Setup
localai.content:
LocalAI is a drop-in OpenAI replacement for local models.

**Setup (Docker):**
```bash
docker run -p 8080:8080 \
  -v $PWD/models:/models \
  localai/localai:latest
```

**Setup (Binary):**
1. Download from [LocalAI releases](https://github.com/mudler/LocalAI/releases)
2. Place models in `./models` directory
3. Run: `./local-ai --port 8080`

**Endpoint:** `http://localhost:8080`.

cherrystudio.title: Cherry Studio API Gateway
cherrystudio.content:
Cherry Studio exposes configured models via its API Gateway.

**Setup:**
1. Download [Cherry Studio](https://cherryai.com)
2. Configure at least one model provider in Settings
3. Go to **Settings** → **API Gateway**
4. Set a port (default varies)
5. Click **Start**
6. Copy the API key shown

**Important:** Enable the API key checkbox and paste the key.

**Endpoint format:** `http://localhost:PORT` (check your gateway settings)
